claims.exact_statement: For K>1 and 0<w<=L, the stationary random-shift vertical and horizontal binary stripe ensembles with phase conductivities 1 and K have homogenized tensors diag(2K/(K+1),(K+1)/2) and diag((K+1)/2,2K/(K+1)). The laws of the complete coefficient maps on a square coupon of side w have total-variation distance at most w/L. For N independent coupons, total variation is at most min(1,Nw/L), and every estimator has worst-case expected operator-norm error at least ((K-1)^2/(4(K+1)))*(1-Nw/L)_+.
assumptions: Continuum scalar steady diffusion equation -div(a grad u)=0 in two dimensions.
Perfectly bonded ideal alternating layers; no interface resistance or non-Fourier effects.
Uniform random phase on the period 2L; coupons are independent draws from one of the two ensembles.
Each coupon observation is a function of its complete coefficient restriction to a square of side w; w<=L.
Supplied contrast bounds are 1<=a<=K and the global phase fraction is exactly one half; hidden scale L is not supplied.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_candidate; proof complete in stated model; priority and novelty unverified
claims.novelty_boundary: The general absence of a uniform quantitative rate under qualitative stationarity/ergodicity is established background. The candidate increment is an explicit high-contrast two-phase laminate pair plus a total-variation/Le Cam lower bound for complete finite local coupon maps. Exact priority was not established; the construction may be a simple known consequence of laminate formulas and coupling.

costs.acquisition: For pixel size h, N complete maps require N*(w/h)^2 coefficient readings, plus calibration/specimen costs. Boundary-response measurements are less informative than the full map and do not evade the bound.
costs.computation: The bound is information-theoretic and survives unlimited local computation. Any local PDE solve must separately charge mesh size, solver tolerance, and runtime. Standard RVE solvers additionally charge realization count, coupon size, corrector regularization, and domain truncation.
costs.unknown_input: A bound on correlation scale L, or measurements reaching that scale, must be supplied/acquired to avoid this ambiguity.

claims.falsifier: For K=100, fabricate 50/50 high/low laminates at stripe width L, rotate by 90 degrees, compare small-coupon maps and large-specimen e1 steady conductivity. The scalar continuum model predicts principal coefficients 200/101 and 101/2. A claimed universal estimator based only on K, phase fraction, N, and w is falsified at the model level whenever L>>Nw; a physical prediction mismatch beyond measured interface/discretization corrections falsifies the ideal Fourier laminate model.
claims.next_gate: Construct a matching isotropic scalar-conductivity pair or an exact elasticity-tensor analogue; then search RVE/non-identifiability literature for the precise TV/Le Cam statement before any priority claim.

claims.exact_statement: Quantitative RVE guarantees in the primary sources inspected require more than a phase fraction: examples assume i.i.d. coefficients, finite-range dependence, or a quantified correlation-decay functional inequality, and charge finite-volume realizations and corrector/PDE solves.
assumptions: Claim is about the inspected algorithms/theorems and their stated source assumptions, not every possible quantitative homogenization method.
claims.status: source-reconstructed prior art; exact scopes retained
claims.novelty_boundary: Established literature summary only; no claim of new result.

finite_check.result: Four exact finite phase enumerations matched discrete TV=(w-1)/L; rational K=100 arithmetic gave H=200/101, M=101/2, gap=9801/202, ratio=10201/400.
finite_check.scope_limit: Finite discrete arithmetic only; not independent proof or validation of continuum homogenization.
